utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: As you are no doubt aware ... [French on English channel]. Is that an indication that something is amiss with the technology? It's fixed now? Very well. The accused Stanisic is not in court and I am going to ask the court deputy to say what the position is in relation to Mr. Stanisic's attendance either in court or for the purposes of viewing the video conference link. Yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the accused is not in court and he will not be in the VTC room today. He's currently in the hospital awaiting his medical examination and we will be receiving a report shortly and will be able to notify the Court as to the results.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We should have had in accordance with the procedures set out a medical certificate by this time. We haven't had it. The explanation, I understand, is that the medical officer is not present at the UNDU and in his absence, the UNDU had to obtain the services of another doctor and that has led to some delay. In view of the fact that this is the first time that the procedures which are established are being put in place, the Chamber has some sympathy and understanding for the problems faced by the UNDU. The Chamber expects, however, that the medical report will on all future occasions be ready and transmitted in a timely manner to it. I do have, however, a form prepared by the deputy commander which addresses the first five or six paragraphs of the new set of procedures and I'd like to ensure that the parties have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's being transmitted -- may we have copies made for the parties, but in the meantime, I'll tell you what it says. It seeks to give effect to the first five or six paragraphs of the new set of procedures set out. First, there is confirmation that, and this is from the deputy commanding officer, Fraser Gilmour, that he met with Mr. Stanisic at 11.55. He confirms that he informed him about the court hearing scheduled for today to begin at 2.15 and that normal arrangements were in place to transport him to the Tribunal. Then Mr. Stanisic indicated that he felt too unwell to attend the court in person. He reminded him that he had a right to be present in the courtroom. Mr. Stanisic was not willing to waive his right to attend court in person. He then reminded Mr. Stanisic that it was still open to him to participate in the proceedings via the video conference link. Mr. Stanisic then indicated that he did not wish to use the video conference link, and following that answer, the medical officer or another qualified officer was called upon to carry out an examination and to submit a report to the Trial Chamber. It is that report which we now await and you have just been given the explanation for its absence at this time. Does any party have any comment to make? Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the circumstances, the Chamber determines that the best course is to adjourn the proceedings until such time as the medical report is transmitted to the registry and forwarded to it. We don't believe that that will be a very long time from now, so the parties should stand by and be ready to be recalled shortly. We are adjourned. --- Break taken at 2.25 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are resumed. We have two statements. One is from the deputy registrar received -- or made at 2.25 p.m. and then subsequent to that, I believe we have a statement or a certificate from the doctor who saw Mr. Stanisic today. Since we have this statement in front of us, I am going to read both of them slowly. I will spare the court deputy the reading. This is from the deputy registrar and I presume this would have been based on a telephone conversation between the deputy registrar and the doctor. It may be that it would be enough just to go to the doctor's certificate since we have that now, but in the interest of completeness, I'll read both. In fact, you can read silently the statement from the deputy registrar, and then I'll read the doctor's certificate. It says, "Before me I see Mr. Stanisic. The patient is suffering of severe colitis with a lot of blood loss and diarrhea. He needs frequently to go to the toilet. He's very weak and sweaty because of the blood loss. Therapy starts today and effect, I hope, will soon be seen. It is not advisable to go to trial today and not follow by video conference link." Then there is something which I thought poor penmanship was a province of lawyers but apparently -- I can't read this. That's the name of the -- but there is something before the name, before the signature. I can't make it out but perhaps it has no effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm informed that it's the initials and the name of the doctor. May I ask first ask for the Prosecution to make submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I really don't have too many comments to make, Your Honour, I rely on the Chamber's reading of the words here, other than to point out that we know from the fitness proceedings that he does -- he cannot have colitis, but I imagine the doctor obviously does not have that much familiarity with him. I think it is probably safe for us to conclude that his pouchitis is acting up and it's not colitis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that in light of the paragraphs 12 and 13 of Your Honours' ruling of this morning, we submit that the proceedings for today should be adjourned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you have submissions on that, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I find myself in a difficult position because I think I like many of the participants here are getting increasingly frustrated with the inability for us to make any progress. I must say though that I am reluctant to simply discard the opinion of this doctor who seems to be suggesting -- I mean when I look at her observations that he's very weak and sweaty, it seems that that seems to be something that can be objectively observable by a trained doctor and she's attributing it to blood loss. It does seem rather serious in light of your protocol. I mean it's obviously the Chamber's decision to make a determination whether or not he's too ill to proceed but I certainly don't feel comfortable in arguing that we should proceed disregarding what this doctor has reported to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: My last remark would be, sorry to interrupt your deliberation, but it's of course significant, I believe, that this is a doctor who previously was not involved in the case and apart from Dr. de Man, Dr. Falke, we have now a third independent doctor who comes to this conclusion, so I think it will just underline my request that in light of paragraphs 12 and 13, there is ample basis for the request to adjourn for today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber thanks the parties for their submissions. In particular we are indebted to Mr. Groome for his frankness which is wholly consistent with the best traditions of the bar as the Prosecutor. The Chamber concludes that it has no alternative but to adjourn the hearing. We take into account the doctor's observations that Mr. Stanisic has to go to the toilet frequently, he's very weak and sweaty because of the loss of blood. We also note that therapy is to start today and the hope is expressed that its effect will soon be seen, but we were given to understand that that therapy would have started yesterday and the registrar might wish to inquire what is happening in that regard. The Chamber therefore determines that Mr. Stanisic is not well enough either to attend court or to participate in proceedings by the video conference link today, and we will adjourn until ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The date of the adjournment, now it could be a matter for discussion. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before you rise -- just before you made -- you set a time for adjournment, it occurs to me that we might be able to make some progress in this case in other ways, I mean there are a number of pending motions. If it would assist the Chamber and the parties tomorrow if Mr. Stanisic is too ill to proceed, if it would assist the Chamber in having the parties discuss and present argument on the different pending motions, it would help the Chamber resolve, that might be a productive use of time and advance us in a material way in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber is considering adjourning until tomorrow not specifically to take up Mr. Groome's suggestion, because I am not personally aware of any motions presenting the kind of difficulty that would benefit from interparty submissions during court. These are matters which the Chamber can decide and will decide with promptness. We will adjourn until tomorrow in the event that Mr. Stanisic is well enough to attend either court or the video conference link. So we are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 9th day of May, 2008 at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.05 p.m.
